## F. The architect's follow-up (section 8), decided

**8.1 Languages and hiding: accepted.** The settings live on the profile, `hidden` is marked per track for the calling profile, and nothing is removed or shifted. Invariant 62 is rewritten, not removed. There is one gap: no task lets a profile set its languages through the new API. Saved settings keep applying from the cutover; setting them arrives with JS-157.

**8.2 A playback's life: accepted, with the 90-second hold window as product behaviour.** It serves "Stop on the TV and carry on from the phone at the same moment" only because a refused Play lists the devices holding playbacks and lets the viewer end one with one press. That is a condition (JS-211). The silent restart rests on JS-219 recording what Media3 does when a link is refused.

**8.3 Allowed sets: accepted.** Sets are marks on titles. An unmarked title is seen only by accounts that see all. Configuration refuses unknown keys. The operator's cost (marking once, by a selector or per title) is accepted: PRODUCT.md says organisation never grants.

**8.4 Rules: accepted.** 32 and 62 as rewritten, 75, and new rules 77 and 78; JS-220 takes 77 and 78.

**Wording fixes:**
1. **JS-185:** my record means today's stress figure, 1,600 viewers (docs/running.md: a pool of 64 "held 1600"). It now reads "at 1,600 viewers".
2. **Progress:** JS-216 declares the place a title shows and marking played by hand; JS-217 alone declares progress reports.
3. **Pictures:** JS-215's criterion now distinguishes pictures from media (below). It does not conflict with the A condition: `private` keeps pictures out of shared caches.

**Final criteria text:**
- **JS-216, criterion 1:** "The contract declares M1's catalog and people: sign-in (its answer naming the account, the profile and the device, with different ids in every example), devices and sign-out, TV approval, Films and Shows, seasons and episodes, a title's details with its versions (a list, of one file today) and its tracks, each with an id that names one track of one file version and says whether it is hidden for the calling profile, chapters and artwork, artwork, Continue watching and taking a title off it, the place a title shows and marking it played or unplayed by hand, and a profile's languages, kept languages and hiding switches (declared until JS-157 serves them). Each has its request, its answer, who may call it, the reasons it can refuse with, and at least one example answer Octave can mock against."
- **JS-217, criterion 1:** "The contract declares playback: starting one with what the device can play and the tracks chosen, or with no position to start at the viewer's place; the answer saying how it plays and why; a track or quality change within the same playback; ending it; its media link, and the link's refusal once the playback has ended, with the action to start again; its progress reports; and the messages a running playback receives. Each has its request, its answer, who may call it, its reasons and an example."
- **JS-219, add:** "What Media3 reports to the app when a link is refused because its playback ended, so that an app can start again with nothing shown to the viewer."
- **JS-185, the stress criterion:** "The read each media request makes of its playback and its access is added to the stress run; its 99th percentile at 1,600 viewers is recorded against today's at 1,600 viewers, and one more than 20% above it comes to the product owner as a brief before merge."
- **JS-185, add:** "A playback lives while its app reports on it; one with no report for 90 seconds has ended, never revives, and its link is refused with that reason and the action to start again. A media request does not keep a playback alive. A play with no position starts at the viewer's place with their picks."
- **JS-215, the criterion from B:** "The web sign-in is accepted on picture routes, whose answers are marked private so no shared cache keeps them, and never on any other media request (a stream, a segment, a subtitle, a font) or a media link."
- **JS-211, final:**
  - Criterion 4 becomes "A stream ends and frees its place at once when its app says it stopped, and otherwise 90 seconds after its last report. A paused playback whose app still holds it counts."
  - Add: "A play refused for the limit lists the account's devices holding playbacks, naming a title only for the viewer's own profile; the viewer can end one from the app, and their play then starts."
- **JS-036, criterion 1:** "Configuration sets, for an account, the access marks it may see or all of them, a rating ceiling, and exceptions adding or removing single titles. A title gets a mark from its own metadata file, or from configuration by its name or by a selector over title facts (kind, rating, genre, year, original language). An unmarked title is seen only by accounts that see all. A show's marks reach its seasons and episodes, so a missing mark on a season never hides or shows its episodes by surprise."
- **JS-036, add:** "No configuration, metadata file or rule can name a place films are kept or a directory: configuration with an unknown key is refused at start, and moving a film to another folder or store changes no answer of TestAccess."
- **JS-157, add:** "A profile reads and sets its listening and reading languages, kept languages and hiding switches through the contract, and every app's track menus follow them, with tracks hidden for the profile marked in details and plans."

**Decision entry, D-20261127-domains-followup:** "The architect's follow-up is accepted: language settings and hiding on the profile, marked per track, nothing removed (62 rewritten); a playback lives while its app reports, ends after 90 seconds of silence, never revives, and a play with no position starts at the place; stream limits count held playbacks, and a refusal lists the devices so the viewer can end one; access sets are marks on titles, an unmarked title is seen only by see-all accounts, and no rule names a place (rules 77, 78). Wording: JS-185 measures at 1,600 viewers; progress reports belong to JS-217; the web sign-in is accepted on picture routes, marked private, and on no other media request. Criteria are amended on JS-216, JS-217, JS-219, JS-185, JS-215, JS-211, JS-036 and JS-157." Serves: "Their languages come first"; "Seeking and resuming just work"; "They see only what they may".

**Owner confirmation:** yes. Treat "pictures by id need a sign-in" as awaiting the owner, since it reverses an owner decision. It blocks nothing before JS-186's Spec, which must not fix picture access until the owner answers.
